licence.name: Non-Professional Driver's License (codes A, A1, B, B1, B2)

note: Read 2026-10-30 in the Land Transportation Office's own driver's manual on its LTMS portal (eLearning, Licensing Information; it says the LTO Citizens Charter prevails where they conflict). A new non-professional driver's licence is issued from 17 (with a parent's or guardian's consent at 17) to a holder of a student-driver's permit of at least one month who has passed the practical driving course and the theoretical and practical examinations; foreigners must be at least 18, which the form can't hold beside a citizen's age, so 17 is held. A new licence is valid five years from the holder's birth date; one with no violation in the five years before it expires is renewed for ten, which isn't held. Fees and Other Charges, New License: for a conductor's or driver's licence an application fee of 100.00 and a licence fee of 585.00, total 685.00, the total held (the student-driver's permit's 250.00 isn't). This replaces wave 8's file held for its age (taken from a 2004 circular on converting foreign licences): the age is now the LTO's own manual's. The professional licence isn't held; the national ID (PhilID) is the ids engine's. No exchange list was read.

sources.title: LTO, LTMS eLearning: Licensing Information / Qualifications and Documentary Requirements / New Driver's License
sources.said: Non-Professional DL A, A1, B, B1, B2 ... At least 17 years old ... Foreigners At least 18 years old ... SP holder for at least one (1) month ... A new DL is valid for five (5) years reckoned from the date of birth of the licensee, unless sooner revoked or suspended.
